title: Prospective Assessment of Quality of Life During Radiotherapy for the Treatment of Gynecological tumors
summary:
This study investigates how radiation therapy affects the well-being of women with cancers of the female reproductive organs. While the treatment can be effective, it often causes side effects such as fatigue, pain, or difficulties in daily life.

The researchers aim to better understand how these problems develop during and after treatment. Participants will complete questionnaires at several time points, for example before treatment and at different times afterward.

The goal is to identify common challenges and improve supportive care for future patients.

interventions.name:
Arm 1 includes all patients receiving radiotherapy as part of routine clinical care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed vulvar, vaginal, cervical, or endometrial cancer
Planned radiotherapy (primary, adjuvant, or palliative)
Ability to provide informed consent and written informed consent
Sufficient German language skills to independently complete the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years
Pregnancy
Inability to provide informed consent (e.g. due to severe psychiatric illness or cognitive impairment)
Insufficient German language skills
Participation in a concurrent interventional study with potential influence on quality of life or study endpoints
